page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features a single dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 physical core and vCPU, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports key instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, but lacks AVX-512 capabilities. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The dedicated AMD EPYC core delivers strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% on stress-ng tests, and average single-threaded performance in gzip compression and Geekbench text processing. However, due to its single-vCPU configuration, multi-core and parallel processing benchmarks are constrained, with Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and ray tracing scores falling into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 21.24 GB/sec and write speeds at 18.37 GB/sec, placing memory performance in the lower percentiles.

From a resource density perspective, the t2d-standard-1 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU execution without the overhead of shared-core scheduling. The trade-off is a highly constrained memory and multi-threaded performance profile. It is suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, text processing, and small-scale development tasks that do not require high memory throughput or parallel execution.
